scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Multiples compare protocols; they don't set a "right" price.
scenes.vo: Fees: everything users pay. Revenue: the part that goes to the protocol or token holders (the rest goes to L.P.s/lenders). Earnings: revenue minus token incentives paid out. Multiples: price-to-fees (P/F), price-to-sales (P/S, on revenue), price-to-earnings (P/E). Use F.D.V. as well as market cap, since unlocks will arrive (6.2). Quality checks: is revenue growing without rising incentives? Is it concentrated in one pool or chain? Does it survive a bear market? Does the token actually receive it (value capture)? Multiples compare protocols; they don't set a "right" price.
scenes.cap: Fees: everything users pay. Revenue: the part that goes to the protocol or token holders (the rest goes to LPs/lenders). Earnings: revenue minus token incentives paid out. Multiples: price-to-fees (P/F), price-to-sales (P/S, on revenue), price-to-earnings (P/E). Use FDV as well as market cap, since unlocks will arrive (6.2). Quality checks: is revenue growing without rising incentives? Is it concentrated in one pool or chain? Does it survive a bear market? Does the token actually receive it (value capture)? Multiples compare protocols; they don't set a "right" price.

scenes.sub: FDV $2B, annual revenue $100M, token incentives $60M → earnings $40M. P/S (FDV) = 20×; P/E (FDV) = 50×. A rival with the same revenue but no incentives has earnings of $100M: at the same FDV its P/E is 20×. Same revenue, very different economics.
scenes.vo: F.D.V. $2B, annual revenue $100M, token incentives $60M to earnings $40M. P/S (F.D.V.) = 20 times ; P/E (F.D.V.) = 50 times . A rival with the same revenue but no incentives has earnings of $100M: at the same F.D.V. its P/E is 20 times . Same revenue, very different economics.
